title: Can I BEAT 5D Chess?
summary: 5D Chess With Multiverse Time Travel (video game): he does seven tutorial puzzles (one per piece type), learns an opening trap, beats the weak built-in engine, then plays and aims to win one real public online game.
rules: Standard pieces on 8x8 boards arranged along a time axis (turns) and timeline axis (alternate universes).
Pieces may move through time to past boards (in any direction a piece could move, counting time/timelines as extra dimensions), creating a new branching timeline.
You may only move on 'present' boards (the latest board of each active timeline); a turn requires moving on enough present boards to advance the 'present' line.
Checks can be delivered across time and timelines; checkmate = no legal multiverse move escapes all checks.
Interface: 'Your turn - White pieces', submit turn button, purple time-travel arrows.
win_condition: Checkmate across the multiverse (video goal: win one real public game).

opponent.name: Puzzles, built-in engine, then a public online player

board.shape_notes: Multiple 8x8 boards laid out in a 2D grid (time horizontally, timelines vertically).
board.theme_notes: Beige/brown and grey-blue boards on grey background, purple time-travel arrows; colours are scene colours.

setup: Standard start on the first board of timeline 0.
events: New timeline created on time travel
current_impl_issues: Current 'timetravel' mode is just 3 rewinds/takebacks - nothing like 5D chess. A faithful remake needs multiverse boards; a simplified 2-timeline version would be closer.
evidence: rules.jsonl entry; frames (visual_b): multiverse timelines, purple arrows, 'Your turn - White pieces'.
